name: Hero
summary: Hero sections for the AhaSlides marketing sites: three heroes, five multi-image heroes, five photo galleries and one page header, each with its own preview, switches and paste-and-run code.
highlights: Fourteen layouts on one page: Hero split, Hero stacked, Hero split form, five multi-image heroes, five Gallery layouts and Page header. Colour, alignment, picture and call-to-action differences are switches on the layout, not separate layouts

Every hero, every Gallery layout and the page header has a White / Vivid Pink surface switch, and Vivid Pink is the default: add the layout's own --brand class (Vivid Pink on the DS Splash background), or leave it off for White. There is no Accent surface

An optional G2 reviews row (the G2 logo in a white card, five stars, 4.8 and the review count), on by default, on the three heroes whose copy block holds the call to action; a G2 reviews switch next to the other switches turns it off on the preview. An optional Reassurance line switch (Off by default) adds one short risk-reducer line under the call to action on the seven heroes whose copy block holds it (Hero split form puts its button in the card, so it has none), above the G2 row

Five multi-image heroes show several photos at once, each a different arrangement and transition: Hero photo stack (fanned cards that spread on hover), Hero bento collage (a square bento of four), Hero image marquee (a full-width row that loops like the Logos strip, with no Pause button, as the Logos strip has none), Hero slideshow (crossfading photos picked with Carousel dots) and Hero floating images (tilted pairs around centred copy). The slideshow dots come from lib/marketing-motion.js, and every movement stops under reduced motion, print and data-aha-motion="off"

Five gallery layouts show a set of photos under a centred page header: Gallery bento grid (a square bento), Gallery masonry (a wall that never crops), Gallery carousel (snapping photos picked with Carousel dots, the same dots as Hero slideshow), Gallery marquee rows (two looping rows, no Pause button) and Gallery tabbed images (tabs that crossfade between photos). Each has a White or Vivid Pink background (Vivid Pink by default), and the carousel dots and the tabs come from lib/marketing-motion.js

One button per layout: the primary call to action (Get started or Sign up), never a second white secondary beside it. No small label or badge above any headline. Every slider uses one style, the DS Carousel dots (16 × 4 px bars, the current one 28 px wide in Vivid Pink, in 24 × 24 px buttons) centred under the photos, with no arrow buttons
layoutsIntro: Each layout is its own block: the class names below are scoped per layout, so any number of them can sit in one page.

guidance.title: Choosing a hero
guidance.intro: Pick the hero from the goal of the page, then check the points below. The layouts further down carry a "Use for" line.

points.title: One goal, one primary button
points.text: Each page has one goal and one primary button: one Vivid Pink primary and no second button beside it. Never two primaries, as the Button rule allows one primary per view. On the Vivid Pink surface the button is variant="secondary"; on White it is the primary. The per-surface switch is the data-variant-<state> hook on the button, so paste the snippet for the surface you use.

points.title: Layout by page goal
points.text: Sign-ups (home, campaign, landing): Hero split or Hero stacked with the Email form call to action. Use Hero split form only when you need more than an email. Feature pages: Hero split with the Bleed picture for a wide screenshot, or Hero stacked when the product screen is the proof. Content and listing pages (blog, templates, help): Page header, with its one Get started button. Brand or campaign banners: any hero on the Vivid Pink surface. Event, community, brand and culture pages with several real photos: the multi-image heroes (Hero photo stack, Hero bento collage, Hero image marquee, Hero slideshow, Hero floating images). Several photos shown as a set, without hero copy beside them: the Gallery layouts. Photos of one shape: Gallery bento grid (square) or Gallery carousel (4:3). Photos of mixed shapes: Gallery masonry, which never crops. One photo per audience or setting: Gallery tabbed images. A big set of mood photos: Gallery marquee rows.

points.title: Copy
points.text: Write an outcome-led headline of about ten words or fewer and a one-sentence lead. Label the button with a verb and the outcome. Put a risk reducer under the button, for example "Free forever. No credit card needed." The Reassurance line switch adds it as one muted line under the button, and only when the claim is true for that page.

points.title: Above the fold
points.text: The headline, the button and the visual are visible without scrolling at 1280 by 720 and on mobile. Use a real AhaSlides screenshot, not a stock photo. No small label or badge sits above the headline. For proof, keep the G2 reviews row (the G2 logo, stars and the 4.8 rating), which sits under the call to action on the heroes and is on by default. In Hero stacked the picture is shown whole at its own ratio at every width, never cropped with object-fit cover (rule W6): supply the screenshot at the ratio you want shown.

points.title: Colour
points.text: Colour rule 3.5 keeps the first screen of a product-app screen white, but a web page built from full-width sections may open with a Vivid Pink hero (it is one of the two Vivid Pink sections of rule 3.4). Follow it with a full white section, never another coloured one. A Vivid Pink hero always carries the DS Splash background (right when the copy is beside a picture or left-aligned with no picture, centre when the copy is centred or a picture fills the width), never a flat pink fill or hand-drawn hooks.

points.title: One H1 per page
points.text: A page has one h1. If a second hero sits on the page, its headline becomes an h2.

points.title: Measure
points.text: Track the click on the primary button. A/B test the headline before you change the layout.

points.title: Background
points.text: Every hero, every Gallery layout and the page header has a White / Vivid Pink switch, and Vivid Pink is the default: add the layout's own --brand class (for example aha-header-section-hero-split--brand) for Vivid Pink on the DS Splash background, or leave it off for White. There is no Accent surface. Never place a Vivid Pink hero next to another coloured section.

points.title: Hero video
points.text: A hero can carry a video instead of the image (the optional Video slot below, off by default): a real <video> with controls, a poster that is a real screenshot, an English captions track and a download link as fallback. It never autoplays, never loops and never starts with sound, so it is safe under prefers-reduced-motion; the native controls are keyboard reachable. The video box is 16:9, so use a 16:9 clip: it fills the box edge to edge with no side bars or bands. A height cap keeps it from taking over the hero; on a wide screen the box narrows and centres instead of letterboxing.

layouts.name: Gallery carousel
layouts.summary: A centred page header, then a row of captioned 4:3 photos, three in view at 1440 (one and a bit on a phone), that snaps photo by photo when swiped or scrolled. video.label: Video slot
video.howToTurnOn: Replace the layout's with the video html and add the css once, replacing {{c}} with the layout class. Use a 16:9 clip and set the width and height attributes to its real pixel size; the slot is 16:9 and crops any other ratio. Off by default: the layout html and css leave it out. Never add autoplay, muted autoplay or loop.
